prize_parts.citation: For the development of palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: I keep B048 as my single-part position after the full round-1 exchange. Palladium-catalysed C-N coupling is a general method whose adoption can be checked in the literature: it is routine in medicinal-chemistry routes, in process-scale manufacture of drugs and agrochemicals, in organic electronic materials and in total synthesis. The chemistry that made it general is specific to this bond. Bulky, electron-rich biaryl phosphines (Buchwald) and hindered alkyl and ferrocenyl phosphines (Hartwig) were designed against the elementary steps that differ from C-C coupling: amine binding and deprotonation at palladium, beta-hydride elimination competing with the desired path, and C-N reductive elimination from an amido complex, which is much harder than C-C reductive elimination. That is a distinct catalyst-design problem, solved independently by two groups over three decades, which gives a clean two-name credit. The Kosugi and Migita tin-amide reactions were stoichiometric in tin and narrow; they were the precedent, not the general catalytic method, and a citation worded around catalytic C-N cross-coupling handles that honestly.
statement.case_against: The weight of round 1 is on B017, which five members now name and which I accept is a strong, mature candidate with real chemistry in it. Against B048: the 2010 prize honoured Pd cross-coupling, so some will read amination as an extension of that family, and Linke's question about what new capability, as opposed to a better ligand set, is being cited is fair. My answer is that before these ligands, aryl amines from aryl halides could not be made reliably under mild conditions, and afterwards they could, for essentially any amine and a wide range of aryl electrophiles, but this is a narrower constituency than sequencing reaches. A prize to a reaction used mainly by chemists will look modest next to a platform used across biology and medicine, and I do not claim otherwise. The Kosugi omission also still needs careful wording.

responses.point: Linke asks what new capability, as opposed to a better ligand set, the committee would be citing in B048, and holds that the 2010 prize already honoured the principle of Pd cross-coupling.
responses.response: The capability is the catalytic formation of aryl C-N bonds from aryl halides and sulfonates with essentially any amine under mild conditions. This was not available before, and the ligand design is how it became available. The obstacle is mechanistic: C-N reductive elimination from an amido palladium complex is slow, and beta-hydride elimination of the amide competes. Overcoming these needed ligand classes (Buchwald's biaryl phosphines, Hartwig's hindered alkyl and ferrocenyl phosphines) that are not predicted by the C-C coupling paradigm. I would call that a second chemical problem, not a refinement. I accept that a reader of the 2010 citation may still see a family resemblance, and I weigh that as a real cost, not as nothing.

responses.point: Aili accepts the strength of the B048 attribution but sees C-N coupling as an expansion of the 2010 framework, while sequencing created a capability that did not exist at scale; he adds that he would be persuaded if the ligand-design principle is a distinct concept.
responses.response: That is the question I would answer, and my answer is that the ligand-design principle is distinct. Ligands tuned for oxidative addition and transmetalation in C-C coupling do not solve amido-palladium reductive elimination, so the field had to find new ligand architectures. Both groups did so on independent routes, with mechanistic work on amine binding and reductive elimination backing the ligand choices. On B017 I grant that the reversible-terminator chemistry is real molecular design, and I do not dispute that it created a new capability at scale. My disagreement is only whether the novelty and clean credit of B048 should be ranked below it.

responses.point: Aqvist proposes Balasubramanian, Klenerman and Mayer for B017, with Ju and Rothberg left out, and says that if the committee cannot defend a third name the Cambridge pair alone is cleaner and B048 would then be justified on cleanliness of attribution.
responses.response: I agree that if no defensible third name emerges, B017 reduces to the Cambridge pair, and then both B017 and B048 are two-name prizes with the same cleanliness question. My reservation on the three-name version is as stated by Chabes and Brzezinski: I cannot see from this record that Mayer's clustering concept was experimentally independent of the Cambridge work, so a seat for him is a priority judgment without evidence. If the committee ends up with Balasubramanian and Klenerman, I would find that a coherent chemical prize. I still prefer B048 because it has no equivalent open priority question.

responses.point: Chabes places B048 outside his top eight and cites novelty relative to 2010, while saying he defers to my view on what amination adds and would not oppose it as a second-tier choice.
responses.response: I appreciate the deference, and I will use it only to say that the chemical addition is the new ligand classes and the mechanistic understanding of amido-palladium reductive elimination. In the other direction, I take Chabes's point about reversible terminators and fluorescent nucleotides as real chemistry, which I granted in round 1, and I take his and Aili's request that a B017 citation state plainly that it is a chemistry prize. I still hold that the Sanger precedent of 1980 weakens the novelty case more than the 2010 precedent weakens B048, because 1980 recognised the readout principle itself.

responses.point: Zou values B048 for clean attribution but would not put it ahead of a materials-and-catalysis achievement (B041) with no recent prize in its area.
responses.response: I accept that no recent prize covers zeolite catalysts, and that Zou knows the structure-function evidence far better than I do. My concern remains that B041 names a field and not one decisive step. Corma's active-site engineering, Zones and Davis on structure-directing agents, and Yu and Tsapatsis on frameworks are distinct advances, and any three-name cut is a choice among them. For B048 the credited step and the people are the same thing.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will treat C-N coupling as a distinct achievement or as an extension of the 2010 prize, which I cannot settle by argument alone.

Whether the citation should name catalytic C-N cross-coupling in a way that adequately handles Kosugi and Migita, and how Buchwald's and Hartwig's first catalytic examples should be sequenced if the committee asks for it.
Whether B017 can be given a defensible laureate set (Cambridge pair with or without Mayer) given the Ju and Rothberg claims, since that decides whether it is a better configuration than mine.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict. I have no personal, collaborative or institutional tie to Buchwald, Hartwig, Kosugi or any other named candidate on the shortlist. My Masamune/MIT postdoc connection does not extend to them. As a synthetic organic chemist I use Pd cross-coupling in my own work, which is field proximity and not a conflict. Lund colleagueship with Linke and Sparr is not a recusal issue, and nothing has changed since round 1.
